mcqs.question: Two convex lenses are used separately with the same object placed to the left of each lens. Lens A has a focal length of 10 cm and the object is 30 cm from the lens. Lens B has a focal length of 5 cm and the object is 20 cm from the lens. Which setup yields the larger magnitude of linear magnification?

options.A: Lens A (f = 10 cm, object distance = 30 cm) gives the larger magnification.
options.B: Lens B (f = 5 cm, object distance = 20 cm) gives the larger magnification.
options.C: Both lenses give the same magnitude of magnification.
options.D: Neither lens forms a real image, so magnification cannot be compared.

mcqs.answer: Lens A (f = 10 cm, object distance = 30 cm) gives the larger magnification.
mcqs.explanation: Using the Cartesian sign convention, for Lens A: 1/10 = 1/v - 1/30 → v = 7.5 cm, magnification m = v/u = 7.5/(-30) = -0.25 (|m| = 0.25). For Lens B: 1/5 = 1/v - 1/20 → v = 4 cm, m = 4/(-20) = -0.20 (|m| = 0.20). Since 0.25 > 0.20, Lens A gives the larger magnitude of magnification.

mcqs.question: In the context of thin lenses, which of the following statements correctly defines the optical power of a lens?

options.A: Power is the reciprocal of the focal length measured in metres.
options.B: Power is the product of the focal length and the refractive index of the lens material.
options.C: Power is the ratio of the image distance to the object distance.
options.D: Power is the difference between the object distance and the image distance.

mcqs.answer: Power is the reciprocal of the focal length measured in metres.
mcqs.explanation: The optical power P of a thin lens is defined as P = 1/f, where f is the focal length in metres. The unit is dioptre (D). Options B, C, and D describe unrelated quantities.

mcqs.question: A convex lens has a focal length of 20 cm. What is its power in dioptres?
mcqs.explanation: Convert focal length to metres: 20 cm = 0.20 m. Power P = 1/f = 1/0.20 = 5 dioptres. Hence option B is correct.

mcqs.learning_point: Understand combination of lens powers at the required level
mcqs.question: Two thin lenses are placed in contact. Lens 1 has a power of +2 D and Lens 2 has a power of +3 D. What is the resultant power of the combination?
mcqs.explanation: When thin lenses are in contact, their powers add algebraically: P_total = P1 + P2 = +2 D + +3 D = +5 D. Therefore the combination has a power of +5 dioptres.

mcqs.question: Which of the following equations correctly represents the lens formula using the Cartesian sign convention?
mcqs.explanation: With the Cartesian sign convention, object distance u is taken negative, image distance v positive for real images, and focal length f positive for convex lenses. The correct form is 1/f = 1/v - 1/u. Option B omits the sign change, while C and D are not the lens formula.

mcqs.question: An object is placed 15 cm to the left of a convex lens whose focal length is 10 cm. Using the Cartesian sign convention, what is the image distance from the lens?

options.A: 30 cm on the opposite side of the lens
options.B: -30 cm on the same side as the object
options.C: 5 cm on the opposite side of the lens

mcqs.answer: 30 cm on the opposite side of the lens
mcqs.explanation: Take u = -15 cm, f = +10 cm. Lens formula: 1/f = 1/v - 1/u → 0.1 = 1/v + 0.0667 → 1/v = 0.0333 → v = +30 cm. Positive v indicates a real image on the opposite side of the lens, 30 cm away.

mcqs.question: A convex lens of focal length 12.5 cm forms an image of an object placed 25 cm from the lens. What is the linear magnification of the image?
mcqs.explanation: Using u = -25 cm, f = +12.5 cm: 1/f = 1/v - 1/u → 0.08 = 1/v + 0.04 → 1/v = 0.04 → v = +25 cm. Magnification m = v/u = 25/(-25) = -1. The negative sign indicates an inverted image of the same size.

mcqs.question: A student uses a convex lens with a focal length of 0.20 m to focus sunlight onto a piece of paper. What is the optical power of this lens?
mcqs.explanation: Power P = 1/f, where f = 0.20 m. Hence P = 1/0.20 = 5 D. The other options correspond to incorrect inverses or misplacements of the decimal point.
